newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs rally on weak output data, rate fears remain.
newsitem.headline: JGBs rally on weak output data, rate fears remain.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures recouped early losses to end sharply higher on Thursday.

Weaker-than-expected industrial production data for April released this afternoon triggered hectic buying back, but the topside was capped due to lingering concerns that Japan may raise interest rates some time this year, traders said.
The Trade Ministry said industrial production fell 0.4 percent in April from the previous month, compared with the ministry's earlier forecast of a 0.3 percent rise.
The key June contract ended up 0.60 at 123.50.
The contract hit a session high of 123.59. It jumped more than 0.70 from around 122.80 just before the output figures came out at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
"The market was surprised by the April figure and the forecast for the April-June period. Both were much worse than expected," said a senior dealer at a "Big Four" brokerage.

Economists polled by Reuters had predicted April output would rise despite the April 1 rise in Japan's sales tax, with forecasts ranging from a 0.3 percent to 1.5 percent increase, compared with a month-on-month drop of 0.3 percent in March.
The Trade Ministry also said output in the April-June quarter was expected to fall 0.7 percent quarter-on-quarter, against the ministry's earlier forecast of a 0.4 percent fall.

"Earlier today, the market started to factor in a 0.5 point rise in the discount rate, with the June contract's fall toward 120 yen in sight. But the output figures made us stop and rethink the timing of a rate hike," the dealer said.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) announcement late on Wednesday that it would release the next "tankan" corporate sentiment survey on June 25 rather than in early July led to some speculation that interest rates may rise earlier than expected, traders said.

"Speculation was that the next tankan will be released early because the BOJ sees an improvement in corporate sentiment -- opposite from what happened in the last survey," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. "If so, that could justify a rise in the discount rate in July at the earliest."

Traders said a delay in the release of the last tankan was probably timed to prevent weak sentiment as shown in the survey from affecting Japanese corporations' book closings. The last survey was released on April 2.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.630 percent at 0722 GMT, down 0.055 from Wednesday's close.
The yield moved within a wide range of 2.605 and 2.750 percent.

Traders said buying from some institutional investors was detected in the long-end of the JGB yield curve before midday, and that suggested not all operators had speculated on an early rise in the BOJ's discount rate.

"The June's recent fall (before the April output data) was not only due to fears of higher interest rates, but also due to options-related speculative selling," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.
June futures options contracts will expire on Friday.
